languages.name: Lua
languages.description: Expanded Lua reference covering core syntax, tables, functions, metatables, coroutines, modules, and standard libraries for embedded scripting.

categories.name: Core Language
categories.description: Bindings, values, control flow, and operators.

entries.title: local variables
entries.summary: Declare variables with local scope.
entries.definition: Declare variables with local scope.
entries.mental_model: local keeps names scoped to the current block/function rather than the global environment.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local project = "WynCommand"
print(project)
examples.explanation: Declares and prints a local variable.

entries.title: Value types
entries.summary: Lua values include nil, boolean, number, string, function, userdata, thread, and table.
entries.definition: Lua values include nil, boolean, number, string, function, userdata, thread, and table.
entries.mental_model: Lua is dynamically typed: values have types, variables do not.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
print(type(42))
print(type({}))
print(type(function() end))

entries.title: if / elseif / else
entries.summary: Select branches using truthy conditions.
entries.signature: if cond then ... elseif ... else ... end
entries.definition: Select branches using truthy conditions.
entries.mental_model: Only false and nil are falsey in Lua.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local n = 6
if n > 6 then print("many") elseif n == 6 then print("six") else print("few") end

entries.title: numeric for
entries.summary: Iterate across numeric ranges with optional step.
entries.signature: for i = start, stop, step do ... end
entries.definition: Iterate across numeric ranges with optional step.
entries.mental_model: Compact counter loop with inclusive stop.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
for i = 1, 3 do
  print(i)
end

entries.title: generic for
entries.summary: Iterate using iterator functions such as pairs and ipairs.
entries.signature: for k, v in iterator do ... end
entries.definition: Iterate using iterator functions such as pairs and ipairs.
entries.mental_model: The iterator controls how successive values are produced.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
for i, name in ipairs({"Lua", "Wren"}) do
  print(i, name)
end

entries.title: while and repeat
entries.summary: Repeat with pre-test while or post-test repeat/until loops.
entries.signature: while cond do ... end / repeat ... until cond
entries.definition: Repeat with pre-test while or post-test repeat/until loops.
entries.mental_model: repeat always executes its body at least once.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local n = 0
repeat
  n = n + 1
until n == 3

entries.title: multiple assignment
entries.summary: Assign multiple values in parallel.
entries.definition: Assign multiple values in parallel.
entries.mental_model: Right-hand values are evaluated before assignment.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local a, b = 1, 2
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)

entries.title: multiple return values
entries.summary: Functions may return multiple values that callers can capture separately.
entries.definition: Functions may return multiple values that callers can capture separately.
entries.mental_model: Multiple values are a built-in calling convention feature.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local function split() return "M1", "Python" end
local key, language = split()
print(key, language)

categories.name: Functions and Closures
categories.description: Callable values, varargs, closures, and method syntax.

entries.title: Functions
entries.summary: Define named or anonymous first-class functions.
entries.definition: Define named or anonymous first-class functions.
entries.mental_model: Functions are ordinary values that can be stored and passed around.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local function double(x)
  return x * 2
end
print(double(21))

entries.title: Anonymous functions
entries.summary: Create function expressions without names.
entries.definition: Create function expressions without names.
entries.mental_model: Behavior as a value.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local twice = function(x) return x * 2 end
print(twice(21))

entries.title: Closures
entries.summary: Functions capture lexical variables from surrounding scopes.
entries.definition: Functions capture lexical variables from surrounding scopes.
entries.mental_model: The function carries references to lexical upvalues.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local factor = 2
local function scale(x) return x * factor end
print(scale(21))

entries.title: Varargs
entries.summary: Accept a variable number of arguments using ....
entries.definition: Accept a variable number of arguments using ....
entries.mental_model: ... represents the current function's extra argument list.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local function count(...)
  return select("#", ...)
end
print(count(1,2,3))

entries.title: Colon method syntax
entries.summary: Pass the table/object as implicit self when defining or calling methods with :.
entries.definition: Pass the table/object as implicit self when defining or calling methods with :.
entries.mental_model: obj:method(x) is sugar for obj.method(obj, x).

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local Tool = {}
function Tool:label() return self.name end
Tool.name = "Lua"
print(Tool:label())
examples.explanation: Calls a method with implicit self.

entries.title: Table construction
entries.summary: Create array-like, map-like, or mixed tables.
entries.definition: Create array-like, map-like, or mixed tables.
entries.mental_model: Tables are Lua's main mutable data structure.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local macro = { key = "M1", language = "Python", "first" }
print(macro.key, macro[1])

entries.title: pairs()
entries.summary: Iterate over table key-value pairs.
entries.definition: Iterate over table key-value pairs.
entries.mental_model: General table iteration without ordering guarantees.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local t = {a = 1, b = 2}
for k, v in pairs(t) do print(k, v) end

entries.title: ipairs()
entries.summary: Iterate integer keys starting at 1 until the first missing index.
entries.definition: Iterate integer keys starting at 1 until the first missing index.
entries.mental_model: Designed for dense 1-based array sequences.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: for i, v in ipairs({"a", "b"}) do print(i, v) end

entries.title: table.insert()
entries.summary: Insert a value into a sequence-like table.
entries.definition: Insert a value into a sequence-like table.
entries.mental_model: Shift elements to make room when inserting in the middle.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local xs = {"M1", "M3"}
table.insert(xs, 2, "M2")

entries.title: table.remove()
entries.summary: Remove and return an element from a sequence-like table.
entries.definition: Remove and return an element from a sequence-like table.
entries.mental_model: Delete one sequence slot and compact following elements.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: table.concat()
entries.summary: Join sequence elements into a string.
entries.definition: Join sequence elements into a string.
entries.mental_model: Stitch sequence strings together efficiently.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local words = {"Trans", "Rights", "are", "Human", "Rights"}
print(table.concat(words, " "))

entries.title: table.sort()
entries.summary: Sort a sequence in place with optional comparator.
entries.definition: Sort a sequence in place with optional comparator.
entries.mental_model: In-place ordering of array-like table elements.

examples.title: Example

categories.name: Metatables and Metamethods
categories.description: Customize table behavior and build prototype-like objects.

entries.title: setmetatable()
entries.summary: Attach a metatable that controls special operations for a table.
entries.definition: Attach a metatable that controls special operations for a table.
entries.mental_model: A metatable is a behavior policy attached to another table.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Falls back to the metatable __index table.

entries.title: __index
entries.summary: Control fallback lookup for missing table keys.
entries.definition: Control fallback lookup for missing table keys.
entries.mental_model: Prototype/default lookup hook.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: __newindex
entries.summary: Intercept writes to absent keys.
entries.definition: Intercept writes to absent keys.
entries.mental_model: A write hook used for proxies and validation.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local t = setmetatable({}, { __newindex = function(_, k, v) print(k, v) end })
t.answer = 42

entries.title: __call
entries.summary: Allow a table to behave like a callable function.
entries.definition: Allow a table to behave like a callable function.
entries.mental_model: Metamethods let operators dispatch to table-defined behavior.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local t = setmetatable({}, { __call = function(_, x) return x * 2 end })
print(t(21))
examples.explanation: Calls a table as a function.

entries.title: __tostring
entries.summary: Customize tostring() output for a table/userdata.
entries.definition: Customize tostring() output for a table/userdata.
entries.mental_model: A printable representation hook.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local t = setmetatable({name="Wyn"}, { __tostring = function(x) return "User(" .. x.name .. ")" end })
print(t)

entries.title: coroutine.create()
entries.summary: Create a suspended coroutine from a function.
entries.definition: Create a suspended coroutine from a function.
entries.mental_model: A coroutine is a resumable execution context.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local co = coroutine.create(function() print("inside") end)
coroutine.resume(co)

entries.title: coroutine.yield()
entries.summary: Suspend the running coroutine and optionally pass values to its resumer.
entries.definition: Suspend the running coroutine and optionally pass values to its resumer.
entries.mental_model: Cooperative suspension under program control.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local co = coroutine.create(function() coroutine.yield("paused"); return "done" end)
print(coroutine.resume(co))
print(coroutine.resume(co))

entries.title: error()
entries.summary: Raise a Lua error and unwind until protected handling is found.
entries.definition: Raise a Lua error and unwind until protected handling is found.
entries.mental_model: Abort the current call chain with an error object/message.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: local function fail() error("nope") end

entries.title: pcall()
entries.summary: Call a function in protected mode and capture success/failure as return values.
entries.definition: Call a function in protected mode and capture success/failure as return values.
entries.mental_model: Convert thrown errors into ordinary return values.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local ok, value = pcall(function() return 21 * 2 end)
print(ok, value)

categories.name: Modules and Standard Libraries
categories.description: Code loading and common library functions.

packages.name: package
packages.description: Lua module search paths and require behavior.

entries.title: require()
entries.summary: Load a module once and return its exported value.
entries.definition: Load a module once and return its exported value.
entries.mental_model: Search configured module paths, execute the module, cache the result.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: local json = require("json")

entries.title: package.path
entries.summary: Configure Lua source module search patterns.
entries.definition: Configure Lua source module search patterns.
entries.mental_model: A semicolon-separated template list used by require.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: package.path = package.path .. ";./scripts/?.lua"
examples.explanation: Adds a local script path pattern.

packages.name: string
packages.description: Pattern matching, formatting, slicing, and case conversion.

entries.title: string.format()
entries.summary: Create formatted strings using printf-like placeholders.
entries.definition: Create formatted strings using printf-like placeholders.
entries.mental_model: Template-driven string construction.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: print(string.format("M%d = %s", 4, "Zig"))

entries.title: string.match()
entries.summary: Extract the first substring matching a Lua pattern.
entries.definition: Extract the first substring matching a Lua pattern.
entries.mental_model: Lightweight pattern matching over strings.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local word = string.match("macro=M4", "M%d")
print(word)

entries.title: string.gsub()
entries.summary: Replace substrings matching a Lua pattern.
entries.definition: Replace substrings matching a Lua pattern.
entries.mental_model: Pattern-based global substitution plus replacement count.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local s = string.gsub("hello bat", "bat", "Wyn")
print(s)

entries.title: math.floor()
entries.summary: Round a number downward to the nearest integer.
entries.definition: Round a number downward to the nearest integer.
entries.mental_model: Floor toward negative infinity.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: print(math.floor(3.9))

entries.title: math.random()
entries.summary: Generate pseudo-random numbers using the implementation's PRNG.
entries.definition: Generate pseudo-random numbers using the implementation's PRNG.
entries.mental_model: Convenience pseudo-random generation, not cryptographic randomness.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: print(math.random(1, 6))
examples.explanation: Generates an integer in the requested range.

packages.name: io
packages.description: File handles and simple input/output helpers.

entries.title: io.open()
entries.summary: Open a file and return a file handle or error information.
entries.definition: Open a file and return a file handle or error information.
entries.mental_model: Manual handle-based file I/O.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local f, err = io.open("out.txt", "w")
if f then f:write("Wyn\n"); f:close() end

packages.name: os
packages.description: Environment, time, process and filesystem-adjacent helpers.

entries.title: os.getenv()
entries.summary: Read an environment variable.
entries.definition: Read an environment variable.
entries.mental_model: Expose process environment values to scripts.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: print(os.getenv("HOME"))

entries.title: os.execute()
entries.summary: Execute an operating-system command through the host shell/environment.
entries.definition: Execute an operating-system command through the host shell/environment.
entries.mental_model: Simple process launching with platform-dependent details.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
local ok = os.execute("git --version")
print(ok)
